note: These are supporting places in a historically documented station sequence, not confirmed stops on an operating Johannesburg–Cape Town passenger service. Attractions and visitor activities require their own access checks.

stops.name: Krugersdorp
stops.story: After Johannesburg Park, Krugersdorp is the first named station in the historical sequence. Rails & Roots uses it to show Lerato that the long-distance story has begun beyond the Johannesburg interchange.

stops.name: Potchefstroom
stops.story: Potchefstroom is the next recorded station. Instead of letting its name disappear from the route map, the guide marks it as a place a traveller could research and save for a separate visit.

stops.name: Klerksdorp
stops.story: The historical route continues through Klerksdorp. Its profile gives the journey continuity and leaves space for a more detailed local story once its attractions have been checked.

stops.name: Bloemhof
stops.story: Bloemhof is another named station before the route reaches Christiana. Seeing it on the map reminds Lerato that smaller places are part of the journey too.

stops.name: Christiana
stops.story: Christiana follows Bloemhof in the recorded station order. Rails & Roots keeps it visible without inventing a sightseeing stop or a current departure.

stops.name: Warrenton
stops.story: Warrenton brings the simulated route towards Kimberley. Northern Cape tourism information identifies the town among places on the region's tourism routes, giving Lerato a reason to consider a separately planned visit.

stops.name: De Aar
stops.story: After featured Kimberley, De Aar keeps the railway story moving. Northern Cape tourism describes it as a town on major railway connections; its wider story deserves its own visit rather than an invented train excursion.

stops.name: Hutchinson
stops.story: Hutchinson appears between De Aar and Beaufort West in the historical station list. Its recorded place on the journey is the fact we can present; a visitor attraction has not yet been verified.

stops.name: Laingsburg
stops.story: After featured Beaufort West, the historical sequence reaches Laingsburg. Rails & Roots marks this transition through the Karoo and invites further local research before recommending a specific visit.

stops.name: Matjiesfontein
stops.story: Matjiesfontein remains a supporting stop, but its railway history makes it memorable. Its own visitor information describes a railway museum associated with the station; that museum is a separate experience to plan and verify.

stops.name: Worcester
stops.story: Worcester is one of the final inland places in the recorded route. Its wider area has a documented wine and olive tourism route that a traveller might save for a future, separately planned visit.

stops.name: Wellington
stops.story: The historical journey continues through Wellington. The area's published wine route shows one possible reason to return, with access and individual venues checked when planning an actual trip.

stops.name: Huguenot
stops.story: Huguenot is listed between Wellington and Bellville in the historical source. Rails & Roots preserves the source's station name without claiming a current passenger stop, station entrance or sightseeing connection.

stops.name: Bellville
stops.story: Bellville is the final named station before Cape Town in this historical sequence. It signals that Lerato is nearing the destination of the simulated journey.
